conviction_note: No company-level number the market lacks turned up. Every finding is a peer or macro proxy, and the PNC-specific ones are small: higher, steeper reinvestment yields since the July guide (the 5y is up about 76bp, and management tied 2027 NII to curve steepness), middle-market advisory at peers ran better than PNC's guided -20% QoQ for capital markets, and commercial credit wobbled at WFC. They net to +0.4. The scaled number is (2*0.55-1)*2.5 = +0.25. It sits on abs_move 2.5, between the 3.23% implied and the 0.92% median history, because the Q4 guide is a new period. p_up is held at 55 because the evidence is proxies and PNC has sold or damped its own beats (Q2 EPS $4.85 vs about $4.43 bought +0.9%).
bar: There are two bars. The company's Q3 guide (vs 2Q26): NII +3-3.5% on $4,107M, so about $4,230-4,250M; fee income -5 to -5.5% on $2,279M; other noninterest income $150-200M; adjusted expense -2 to -3% on $3,837M; NCOs about $225M. Source: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000713676/000162828026048308/a2q26earningsslides_vf.htm (2026-07-15). My own arithmetic from that guide gives revenue about $6.57B and adjusted EPS about $4.89. Street consensus EPS: $4.88 (TickerLeague, 12 analysts), $4.91 (Benzinga), $4.97 (Zacks), revenue about $6.6B; aggregated via a WebSearch snippet, https://tickerleague.com/companies/PNC/estimates. Consensus sits at or slightly above the guide. print_vs_bar_pct is measured on revenue against the $6.6B consensus.
positioning_check: Short interest is about 7.0-7.7M shares, roughly 1.8% of about 400M shares, with days to cover 2.8-4.0. Sources: Equibles, 7.2M and 4.0 DTC as of 2026-08-19 (https://equibles.com/stocks/PNC); CurvedTrading, about 7.7M and 2.8 DTC per FINRA 2026-06-30, borrow fee 0.3% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/pnc/). Not a crowded short. Skew is -0.74 vol points (balanced, slightly call-bid) and put/call OI is 1.1. The stock is -7.57% over 20 days, -16.7% from its 52-week high and -12.6% since the July print (Unusual Whales, as of 2026-10-06). No directional statement from the option market to beat.

findings.finding: Since PNC gave its Q3/FY26 guide on 2026-07-15, rates have repriced sharply. Treasury 5y went from 4.24% (2026-07-01) to 5.00% (2026-10-13) and 10y from 4.48% to 5.21%, the 2s10s steepened from about 31bp to about 42bp, and the FOMC hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, a scenario the guide did not assume. On the Q2 call management said PNC is roughly rate-neutral (+/-25bp has 'very little impact to 2026') and that fixed-rate asset repricing plus curve steepness drive 2027 NII. That sets up a constructive 2027 NII and NIM commentary on the call. Netted against the AOCI/tangible-book hit the same yield rise causes on the securities book.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guidance line has moved PNC most. Q3 2025 fell 3.9% on a weak outlook and the 2026-01-16 print, which carried the first FY26 guide, rose 3.79%. Quarters with in-line guides moved 0.05-0.93% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The rate move is public. How it translates into PNC's Q4 guide and 2027 NII run-rate is not, because PNC has not spoken since July: there was no 8-K or Reg FD update after the 2026-09-14 Barclays appearance. If the market were already paying for 2027 NII upside from the steeper curve, PNC would not be -12.6% since the print and -16.7% off its high with balanced skew. The drawdown more likely reflects the TBV/AOCI hit and multiple compression from higher rates, which the call can offset with NII commentary.
findings.independence: Fed hike: https://www.federalreserve.gov/newsevents/pressreleases/monetary20260916a.htm (2026-09-16). Management's rate-sensitivity remarks: https://www.marketbeat.com/earnings/reports/2026-7-15-the-pnc-financial-services-group-inc-stock/ (Q2 call transcript). July yields: https://home.treasury.gov/resource-center/data-chart-center/interest-rates/TextView?type=daily_treasury_yield_curve&field_tdr_date_value_month=202607. The caveat runs the other way: the same yield rise lowers AFS marks and tangible book, which is netted into this size and not filed separately.

findings.finding: PNC guided Q3 capital markets revenue down about 20% QoQ after a pulled-forward Q2. Peers that reported 2026-10-13/14 show the middle-market advisory line holding up better. WFC Commercial Banking clients' investment banking and markets fees rose 25% and WFC CIB M&A revenue rose 30%. JPM IB fees fell only 8% QoQ (+14% YoY). BAC IB fees fell 15.9% QoQ. The fee-income line is the one most likely to beat the -5 to -5.5% guide.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 fees rose 10% QoQ on capital markets and the EPS beat was large ($4.85 vs about $4.43), yet the stock gained only +0.9% (baseline 2026-07-15 and https://www.benzinga.com/quote/PNC/earnings-forecasts). This name damps fee-driven beats.
findings.why_not_priced: Consensus EPS ($4.88-4.97) already sits at or above the guide-implied ~$4.89, so some fee beat is in the bar. What is not in it is the peers' middle-market strength, which postdates most estimate revisions (Zacks says its number was revised down last week). If it were priced, estimates would have moved up into the print rather than down.
findings.independence: JPM 3Q26 narrative, IB fees -8% QoQ: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfexhibit991narrative.htm (2026-10-13). BAC 3Q26 supplement, IB fees -15.9% QoQ, which points the other way: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000070858/000007085826000481/bac-09302026ex993.htm (2026-10-14). PNC's own -20% guide: Q2 call transcript at marketbeat (above). All of this is peer proxy; PNC (Harris Williams) has not confirmed anything since July.

findings.finding: Commercial credit softened at peers in Q3. WFC's commercial NCO rate rose to 0.18% from 0.10% on higher CRE and C&I charge-offs, and its provision rose 13% QoQ on C&I allowance. JPM built $539M of reserves, mostly in Wholesale. Evercore cut its PNC target to $265 from $285 on 2026-10-01, citing caution on expenses and asset quality. PNC's guide of NCOs about $225M on a commercial-heavy book is the line at risk.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: There is no clean PNC precedent in the 8-print baseline. The sector analogue: credit surprises at mid-size lenders in Oct 2025 drove KRE -6% in a day (benzinga, 2025). PNC's NCOs have run at about 25bp, inside guide, for several quarters.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The stock is -12.6% since July and Evercore's note is public. What is unpriced is whether PNC's commercial book follows WFC's NCO step-up. A priced credit scare would show up as positive put skew, and the skew is -0.74, balanced.
findings.independence: JPM: wholesale reserve build $539M, but wholesale NCOs fell, which cuts against this finding; size shrunk for it. https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000019617/000162828026065582/a3q26erfexhibit991narrative.htm. Evercore: https://pluang.com/en/news-feed/outlook-saham-pnc-analisis-rating-dan-target-harga (2026-10-01, single secondary source). WFC also reported nonperforming assets down $585M, which cuts against this finding. Short interest is about 1.8% of float, not crowded.

findings.finding: Loan growth for Q3 is inside PNC's +1-2% QoQ guide. The Fed H.8 shows all-bank loans and leases +6.0% annualized in Q3 2026 (about 1.5% QoQ), with C&I +7.4% annualized, down from 14.7% in Q2. Big-bank commercial balances were roughly flat: BAC average commercial loans +0.7% QoQ, WFC Commercial Banking plus CIB about flat, JPM wholesale flat QoQ.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: In Q2 2026 loans grew 4% against a lower guide. The stock rose +0.9%, and management said the loan growth capped NIM.
findings.why_not_priced: It is priced. It lands inside the company's own guided range and the H.8 is public weekly. Filed at 0 because it is a sourced fact bearing on the print, not because it moves the stock.
findings.independence: BAC supplement: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000070858/000007085826000481/bac-09302026ex993.htm. WFC release (above). Both point the same way: in line.

baseline_tension: Broadly consistent with the baseline. Skew is balanced (-0.74) and the stock has already de-rated 7.6% in 20 days on a rates shock, so the small positive lean leans against the run-up, as a reassurance trade, not with it. The evidence is too proxy-based to lean further than p_up 55.
lessons_applied: Lesson 1 (verified fact is not a predicted reaction; this name damps beats: Q2's large EPS beat bought +0.9%): fee-beat finding cut from +0.3 to +0.2.

Lessons 3 and 5 (own caveat must reach the number; proxy findings filed small): the credit finding's own independence text cites JPM wholesale NCOs down and WFC NPAs down, so it was cut from -0.3 to -0.2. Short interest was checked first: not crowded.
Lesson 6 (bar): the bar rests on the company guide plus three estimates ($4.88-4.97) that roughly agree, so no cap was needed. The loan-growth finding lands inside the guide and stays at 0.
abs_move nudged from 2.3 to 2.5 because the Q4/forward guide is new-period information (core table: guidance change likely, abs up; LESSONS item 8 on understatement). p_up left at 55.
